correctness.rationale: For the positive Brusselator, s=x+y satisfies sdot=A-x=(A-s)+y; bounded complete positive trajectories obey s(t)-A=∫_{-∞}^t exp(-(t-u)) y(u)du>0. Invariance tested against all smooth antiderivatives of s gives E[x|s]=A; against all antiderivatives of y gives B E[x|y]=y E[x²|y]. Positivity yields the conditional variance formula m(B/y-m), with m=E[x|y]>0. Bias dν=(x/A)dμ leads to Eν[x|y]=B/y. E[x|s]=A implies Cov(x,s)=0, hence Var(y)-Var(s)=Var(x)=E[(sdot)²]. If zero, x=A throughout invariant support, and xdot=0 forces y=B/A. Other invariant measures must have positive mass on both sides of x=A. Correctness for compact support in strictly positive quadrant; no extrapolation to boundary or stochastic model.
